core.title: Component URNs are case-sensitive: store and reuse them exactly as written
core.given: A component URN is stored or referenced
core.then: Treat component URNs as case-sensitive: store and reuse each one exactly as written.
avoid: Re-casing or case-normalising an existing component URN.
core.why: The graph addresses components case-sensitively, so a re-cased URN points to a different component or to none.
evidence: Every reference to a component URN matches its declared form character for character.
verification: A check compares every stored, referenced or copied component URN with its declared form exactly as written, with no case normalisation.
Exact reuse does not waive the URN's other shape obligations (pattern, per-segment casing, no file extensions, construction via the stack's URN builder); those apply to the reused URN as well.
Detecting reuse needs a new observer that compares referenced component URN strings with their declared forms; this fact is not observable with today's tooling.

values: component URN stored, referenced or copied

fires: A component URN is stored or recorded in any artifact.
An existing component URN is referenced or copied in any artifact.
doesNotFire: No component URN is stored or referenced.

classification.note: Neutral as written; 'component URN' is the neutral artifact kind of the urn group, not a stack name.
Single obligation carried verbatim; names no stack, runtime or file kind.
'The graph' is the neutral component/plan addressing graph, not a stack artifact.
Role-level anti-pattern (re-casing / case-normalising an existing URN); already neutral.
Character-for-character match with the declared form is stack-neutral.
Generic check semantics: exact comparison, no case normalisation; rendered as the first verification entry.
Scoping note: exact reuse waives nothing; the 'pattern, casing, extension, builder' parts are the sibling URN-shape obligations, each realized per stack, so the statement stays neutral.

Task term is neutral and stays in core activation: per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys, rule-specific task terms belong to core activation (neutral) or the realization, not to profile data. The values 'component URN' and 'component:' are carried verbatim.
Change fact is neutral; its observer note (comparing referenced component URN strings with their declared form) is preserved as the third verification entry.

neutralityNotes: This rule is stack-neutral by nature: it constrains plan artifacts and the graph's identifier addressing, not any runtime or code stack, so no item needed a Bun-only split and bunOnly is empty. 'prefer' and 'unless' are empty in bun.json and stay empty (no weakening or strengthening). The core needs no profile data: 'component URN' and the token 'component:' are rule-specific activation task terms, which the vocabulary's notProfileKeys assigns to core activation rather than to profile keys, so profileRequirements is empty (the urn.component shape key is not needed here; the sibling shape obligations are only cross-referenced generically in verification). 'The graph' in 'why' is kept as the neutral addressing graph. The 'builder' mention in verifier_detail[1] refers to the sibling construction obligation (built via the stack's URN builder) and is realized per stack; no vocabulary key is needed for a mere cross-reference. fires/doesNotFire were carried verbatim because they are already role-level.
